foot: Storytime tour v0.1.0. Each picture appears first as a wireframe, then fades into the photograph or record itself. Subtitles light up word by word as they are read. Translations other than English are machine translated and not yet checked by a native speaker. Every scene is built only from evidence-catalogue entries; lines marked “Our reading” are the project's working interpretation.

scenes.title: Beneath the ground
scenes.text: Long before any estate paper, Llandough was lived on: a Roman villa, an early Christian cemetery of over a thousand burials beside the church, and finds later lost in a 1983 fire.

img.caption: EV-0056: Neath Guardian, 17 April 1980: “Roman villa remains at Llandough” (cutting image)

scenes.title: The name Cedwyn
scenes.text: The name Cedwyn runs through the land: Cwm-Cedwyn on the Ely, Nant-Cedwyn, Cwm Cydfin Wood. Our reading: the name is older than the estate papers.

img.caption: The house and yard (family album, context image, not yet catalogued)

scenes.title: Tŷ Mawr on the map
scenes.text: 1824: a survey draws the holding as plan 19, Cedfin or Tŷ Mawr Farm, with a table of its fields. The first mention found so far in the estate surveys.

img.caption: EV-0004: Map of Ty Mawr Dated 1824 (Uploaded Image)

scenes.title: The tithe map
scenes.text: About 1841: the tithe list puts John Williams on 36 parcels, 33 entered against Bute. A tithe list did not test title; our reading is that this Bute entry is the one to scrutinise.

img.caption: EV-0005: Historical map labelled “1841-map” (title, date, source not checked)

scenes.title: Rates and the quarry
scenes.text: 1872 to 1877: rate books name John Williams; an 1877 Bute agreement with a quarry firm touches the house parcel. Our reading: the start of the limeworks carve-up.

img.caption: The yard and barn end (family album, context image)

testimony: The 33 acres taken for the limeworks: a line the project traces; the acreage is not yet in the catalogue

scenes.title: A household of standing
scenes.text: 1881 to 1910: John Williams, farmer, in the census; on the court leet grand jury in 1910. Our reading: a family of standing in the parish.

img.caption: EV-0010: Newspaper report: reported theft of geese from Great House Farm, Llandough (1891)

scenes.title: Woods, drains and estate papers
scenes.text: 1902 to 1931: estate auctions, conveyances and a 1916 estate paper the family contest. Meanwhile the family plant trees, the native custom of asserting ownership.

img.caption: EV-0199: Photograph: tree planting at Great House Farm (date unknown)

scenes.title: Transferred over their heads
scenes.text: 1938 to 1942: the Bute interest passes to Western Ground Rents; a 1939 paper is drawn up in John Williams's name. Our reading: the land changed hands on paper without the family.

img.caption: EV-0023: DBDT123/7 — 1939 agreement, Western Ground Rents to John Williams, with plan

testimony: Wartime smoke-screen vehicles on parcel B from 1939: testimony (1 Nov 2026); no catalogue item yet

scenes.title: The courts begin
scenes.text: 1949 to 1957: an unwritten re-grant, title papers missing from the farmhouse, then the county court. Our reading: occupation recast as permission.

img.caption: The yard and stables (family album, context image)

scenes.title: A Welsh Crichel Down
scenes.text: 1958: Mrs Mary Buckler of Tŷ Mawr calls it a Welsh Crichel Down: land farmed by her family since 1667, wrongfully appropriated.

img.caption: Tŷ Mawr, the front of the house (family album, context image)

scenes.title: Orders, a school and a green
scenes.text: 1959 to 1970: offers, a 1962 order, the school site in 1965, BP in 1969, and parcel C registered as village green in 1970. Our reading: taken a parcel at a time.

img.caption: The entrance gate (family album, context image)

scenes.title: The survey and the open day
scenes.text: 1974: the Royal Commission measures the house; an open day to save it; Mary Williams pleads ownership. 1975: the house moves between BP companies on paper.

img.caption: EV-0048: Daily Telegraph report: 'Open day' to save ancient Welsh house (Ty Mawr, Llandough)

scenes.title: Registered
scenes.text: 1982 to 1983: the land, then the farmhouse, first registered as titles WA231076 and WA240304. Our reading: the registration step in the pattern.

img.caption: The farmhouse, side and porch (family album, context image)

scenes.title: Judgment
scenes.text: 1986 to 1987: High Court, then Court of Appeal, for BP. The local plan still marked the buildings to be retained.

scenes.title: The house comes down
scenes.text: 1988: eviction, then on 7 December bulldozers just after 4 am. By breakfast nothing stood, while listing was still being considered.

img.caption: EV-0086: Newspaper photograph captioned "Police wait outside the farmhouse"

scenes.title: After
scenes.text: 1989 to 1996: building destroyed by owners, the record notes. Houses and a green follow; the 1994 dig finds the early Christian cemetery.

img.caption: EV-0112: "From farm to a bus": South Wales Echo feature by Peter Collins on Billy Buckler

scenes.title: In the law books
scenes.text: 2002 onward: the case becomes a textbook lesson on adverse possession while the land passes on.

img.caption: EV-0084: Photograph: Great House Farm ruins with the church (David Purser Photography)

scenes.title: Asking the record holders
scenes.text: 2026: the record holders are asked directly. Every answer becomes a catalogue entry; every gap a missing record.

img.caption: EV-0146: The National Archives Manorial Documents Register: Llandough Manor Return (HMC 9.311)
